proposed_comments.body:
### Describe the conditional vertical-bar baseline

**Severity:** `low`

The vertical-bar comment says the bars start at zero, but `yMin` can fix a positive displayed minimum and the renderer clamps zero into the displayed range. In that case the bars use the lower axis bound as their baseline. Please make the comment describe this conditional behavior.

```suggestion
            // The baseline is zero when it falls within the displayed range; otherwise it uses the nearest axis bound.
```

confidence.rationale: The fixed-minimum and clamped-baseline behavior is explicit in the pinned source; this is a documentation correction, not an unverified visual claim.

proposed_comments.title: Describe the conditional vertical-bar baseline

proposed_comments.body:
### Include zero in the automatic vertical-bar maximum

**Severity:** `medium`

With vertical values -10 and -5 and no yMin/yMax, this call passes dataMax=-5 to ChartScale.Compute. The resulting range is [-10,-5], so CreateVerticalPlot clamps its baseline to -5 instead of zero. This conflicts with the default zero-baseline behavior described for vertical bars. Include zero in the automatic maximum while preserving an explicit yMax through ChartScale.Compute.

```suggestion
        var range = ChartScale.Compute(_model.YMin, _model.YMax, Math.Min(0, dataMin), Math.Max(0, dataMax));
```

Verify all-negative data without overrides uses a maximum of zero, mixed data still includes zero, and an explicit negative yMax remains unchanged.

confidence.rationale: Exact upstream arithmetic identifies the negative-only default maximum. Both literal candidates passed the original 113-test suite; two added regression cases passed in a separately validated 129-test suite. No rendered interaction claim is made.
